API review is restricted to named read scopes; unchanged long-form source content is inherited explicitly, not claimed as newly read in full.

observations.docs/build-guarantees.md: The old source-only-sounding heading becomes Prepare, review and publish. The explicit semantic marker preserves prepared-publication-from-source.
observations.docs/cards.md: The revised opening correctly separates Basic note front/back fields from the card produced by the stock template. Note::basic stores those fields; schema::stock supplies the Basic template. The two-notes/three-cards example and executable bytes remain unchanged.
observations.docs/de/anki-forge-vs-genanki.md: The media row now explicitly says typed objects manage immutable media-data snapshots. Media owns Arc<Snapshot>; image/sound retain a clone. This does not promise independent clone storage or dependence on source files.
observations.docs/de/build-guarantees.md: Error-kind/code wording now names structured fields correctly; the concurrent-work heading becomes Nebenläufige Vorgänge. The immutable project snapshot and last-temporary-owner lifetime paragraph is preserved, with the old German heading mapped to concurrent-work.
observations.docs/de/concepts.md: The new instruction to retain namespace and record keys when editing or sorting preserves the stable-key identity rule and the distinction from display names. Atomic-add conditions and note/model dependencies are unchanged.
observations.docs/de/csv-to-anki.md: Teilbaren is clarified as a deck that can be passed on. UTF-8 CSV columns id/front/back, Python parsing responsibility, Basic-card export and no-Anki export requirement are unchanged.
observations.docs/de/media.md: Stapelimport is clarified as importing multiple media files, avoiding confusion with Anki decks. Worker count, serial threshold, per-file limits, cleanup/order and GIL/event-loop conditions remain unchanged; the old batch heading still resolves to batch-behavior-and-budgets.
observations.docs/de/node-api.md: The renamed heading describes importing several media files and preparing publication. Public package availability and actual API signatures/consume semantics below it are unchanged; both semantic anchors and the former German heading are retained.
observations.docs/de/python-api.md: The renamed heading describes batch media and publication preparation. It retains source-api-details as the semantic destination and maps the old German heading there. The methods and publication limits are unchanged.
observations.docs/es/anki-forge-vs-genanki.md: The opening now explains that imported media data survives source-file changes and that comparison and risk policy are reviewed before publication. This matches Media snapshot ownership and PreparedPublication, without claiming genanki migration or automatic safety.
observations.docs/es/build-guarantees.md: Trabajadores is narrowed to worker threads. The referenced example, typed-error behavior, close/consumption and late-durability limits are unchanged.
observations.docs/es/updates.md: The title now names updating a deck. The risk paragraph correctly says exceeding inspection limits is a hard failure rather than calling limits themselves errors. Namespace/evidence/candidate hard failures and policy restrictions are unchanged.
observations.docs/ja/build-guarantees.md: The heading and introduction explain preparing a candidate and saving it after review. The unchanged paragraph explicitly states prepare_publication does not replace the destination and publish uses that same candidate; consumption and late-failure limits remain. The old heading alias is preserved.
observations.docs/ja/compatibility.md: Only the link label for the prepare-review-publish workflow changes; its semantic destination and public 0.3.1 statement are unchanged. Runtime/native-target and client-compatibility limits remain inherited.
observations.docs/ja/installation.md: The package feature list replaces the opaque prepared-publication term with advance candidate-file generation. The actual public API supports preparation; install command, Rust 1.92 minimum, empty defaults and native-toolchain caveats are unchanged.
observations.docs/ja/json-to-anki.md: The first output is clarified as the initial distribution APKG and the second as a checked answer-only update. Three notes, three cards, two media, complete SDK programs and no-Anki export requirement are unchanged.
observations.docs/ja/media.md: The opening now gives speech synthesis as an example of an external audio-generation tool, rather than implying it generates images. Media import still copies supplied data and retains immutable snapshots; code and API constraints are unchanged.
observations.docs/ja/node-api.md: The opening no longer falsely suggests Project is the only exported API: it correctly describes composing notes/media around Project. index.ts exports Content, Media, Field and other public classes. Batch/preparation wording and heading are clearer; exact APIs and both semantic anchors are preserved.
observations.docs/ja/python-api.md: Batch/prepared-publication terminology becomes advance generation of candidate files. The subsection still explains prepare/review/publish and consumed-owner behavior, with unchanged methods and source-api-details destination; the old Japanese heading is retained as an alias.
observations.docs/ja/python-migration.md: The old optional-artifact return is correctly described as a return value that may lack an artifact, contrasted with guaranteed BuildOutput and structured errors. No optional API or new behavior is introduced.
observations.docs/ja/rust-api.md: The introduction describes the public API as candidate pre-generation and saving. The unchanged Rust example uses prepare_publication followed by publish; source-only/public-version boundaries and ownership limits are retained.
observations.docs/ja/updates.md: The revised explanation explicitly connects prepare_publication and publish to writing the very APKG reviewed in the report. PreparedPublication owns one private candidate and publish consumes that candidate; no rebuild or client-import guarantee is added.
observations.docs/pt-br/anki-forge-vs-genanki.md: The media row corrects the misleading independent-copies wording: snapshots are independent of original source files, while clones share storage. This matches Arc<Snapshot> and typed Content retention.
observations.docs/pt-br/genanki-migration.md: Media snapshots are now described as independent of source files, and template expressions are distinguished from note-type models and Field keys. Stable business IDs, plain-text/HTML handling, no legacy identity reconstruction and migration boundary remain unchanged.
observations.docs/pt-br/index.md: Card templates consistently use templates while tipos de nota still names note types; the note-fields → templates → cards relationship remains correct. Navigation targets and supported tasks are unchanged.
observations.docs/pt-br/node-quickstart.md: The reusable template-bundle link label changes from modelos to templates, with the same destination. Runtime, npm install command, complete program and TypeScript setup remain byte-identical.
observations.docs/pt-br/python-migration.md: The migration table now says Media snapshots do not depend on source files and calls old template bundles templates. The in-process binding and original APKG evidence requirements are unchanged.
observations.docs/pt-br/python-quickstart.md: Only the template-bundle navigation label changes. Python install/run commands, native-wheel prerequisites, program and expected output are unchanged.
observations.docs/pt-br/troubleshooting.md: The media/template heading and bundle-failure row now distinguish card templates from note-type models. Bundle-v2, stable keys, internal paths and explicit media dependencies remain the repair conditions; the old heading alias is retained.
observations.docs/pt-br/updates.md: The prose distinguishes note types from card templates and clarifies exceeded inspection limits as a hard failure. Original APKG evidence, versioned identity, historical slots/revisions, non-deletion semantics and client validation caveats are unchanged.
observations.docs/python/api.md: Source API details becomes Batch media and prepared publication, matching the already stated public 0.3.1 availability. The explicit source-api-details section marker retains prior links; signatures and behavior are unchanged.
observations.docs/template-bundles.md: Explicit media closure is expanded to all explicitly declared media dependencies, and model declaration is clarified as note type definition. from_bundle snapshots the complete validated bundle and media before returning immutable NoteType; no partial project mutation is implied.
observations.docs/updates.md: Only the page heading changes publication to deck. Stable identities, original distribution baseline, risk-policy conditions, executable examples and client-import limits remain unchanged.
observations.docs/zh-cn/anki-forge-vs-genanki.md: The media row explains immutable data snapshots and clone storage sharing. This agrees with Media Arc<Snapshot>, and does not confuse owning bytes with retaining the original file.
observations.docs/zh-cn/api.md: 身份证据 is clarified as 标识映射与修订信息. IdentityEnvelope/PackageIdentity contain versioned model/note mappings, revisions and media evidence; the original APKG and rejection of Anki re-export remain explicit.
observations.docs/zh-cn/build-guarantees.md: The heading correctly describes preparing a candidate and writing the target after review rather than source-only availability. prepared-publication-from-source is now explicit, and the former Chinese heading maps to it; public version and lifecycle constraints remain.
observations.docs/zh-cn/compatibility.md: The original-APKG condition now calls evidence identifier mappings and revision information. This retains the same necessary baseline data; no broader platform, import or history promise is introduced.
observations.docs/zh-cn/concepts.md: Media now explicitly holds an immutable data snapshot and manages its lifetime. Source independence, shared clone storage and with_export_name preserving prior clones remain correct against Media implementation.
observations.docs/zh-cn/genanki-migration.md: The update paragraph clarifies identity evidence without relaxing the requirement for an original package, identical namespace/keys, or a separately verified legacy-identity migration.
observations.docs/zh-cn/index.md: The opening says APKGs are generated from notes, templates and media files. This is the same capability, with unchanged task links and no scheduling/import claim.
observations.docs/zh-cn/media.md: The single-file import statement now explicitly returns an object holding the media snapshot. Batch concurrency remains opt-in and the four-worker, sixteen-file threshold, per-asset and memory-budget facts are unchanged.
observations.docs/zh-cn/node-api.md: Media.file/bytes now explicitly return Media objects that keep imported data independent of later source-file changes. Node wraps the native handle in immutable Media; signatures, rename behavior, properties and MIME limits remain unchanged.
observations.docs/zh-cn/python-api.md: The file-import row names the returned Media snapshot holder. Source API details is renamed to batch media/prepared publication with an explicit source-api-details marker and old Chinese alias; calls and guarantees are unchanged.
observations.docs/zh-cn/python-diagnostics.md: Missing complete identifier mappings/revision information remains a CompareError hard failure. The wording change does not make evidence corruption a policy-allowable risk or remove completed observations.
observations.docs/zh-cn/python-migration.md: The final prerequisite still requires a complete original distribution APKG carrying current identity/revision evidence. It continues to reject automatic recovery of old bundles or old evidence.
observations.docs/zh-cn/rust-api.md: Consumer applications is clarified as applications using the library. Identity-evidence terminology is clarified in both hard-failure and embedded-evidence passages; public modules, API calls, policy limits and candidate lifecycle are unchanged.
observations.docs/zh-cn/rust-guide.md: Media imports are correctly described as returning snapshot-holding Media objects; image()/sound() are more precisely described as not returning errors. Their signatures return Content directly, while add/build still enforce independent MIME rules.
observations.docs/zh-cn/templates.md: The bundle is explained as note-type definitions, templates, CSS and all declared media dependencies, with stored snapshots. This matches from_bundle validation and immutable NoteType; project atomicity and shared API links remain.
observations.docs/zh-cn/troubleshooting.md: The prerequisite still requires original APKG identity/revision evidence, and neither namespace mismatch nor corrupt evidence can be allowed by a risk policy. Only the explanatory term changes.
observations.docs/zh-cn/updates.md: The opening now separates the versioned evidence format from source-code revision and explicitly retains the original APKG of the preceding distribution. Stable project/note/model/field/template keys and remaining update/client constraints are unchanged.
observations.website/language-briefs.json: Read the three glossary changes: zh-CN identifier/revision evidence agrees with PackageIdentity; pt-BR template de cartão distinguishes Template from NoteType; ja prepared publication is described as candidate generation followed by reviewed saving. Protected API names and product names remain unchanged.

observations.website/src/content/blog/es/stable-ids-a: The baseline heading now says to use the previous package as reference. Its semantic marker and new explicit span preserve the former Spanish slug. Baseline prose, code and distribution-package caveats are unchanged.
observations.website/src/content/blog/ja/stable-ids-a: Relative to the previously reviewed isolated candidate, only the Anki re-export warning is clearer: it cannot be an update baseline. observations.website/src/content/blog/pt-br/stable-id: The title explicitly instructs updating note content without changing its ID. Translation key/date/category, body, code and original distribution baseline condition remain unchanged.
observations.website/src/content/blog/zh-cn/stable-id: The title and final verification paragraph explain stable IDs and matching a note to its prior version. They retain the requirement to inspect source/baseline and not infer correctness from file existence; Anki import/local-edit caveats remain.

observations.website/src/i18n/en.json: Read all changed messages: language controls now explicitly mean programming language; update prose requires original APKG and stable note IDs; AI actions still describe copying a prompt; performance explicitly describes five 1,000-note export tests and the Rust API. observations.website/src/i18n/de.json: Read all changed messages: IDs and original APKG remain required, not-found/examples labels match page actions, and Anki controls final card rendering/import behavior.
